Published p.134, same in arXiv v4: 'Clearly, we can reverse the argument: starting with (E_s^j,∇_s^j), then C(E_s^j,∇_s^j) again is stable and rigid by Lemma 3.4, and thus w^{−1*}C(E_s^j,∇_s^j) as well.' Lemma 3.4 (p.125) is only about w^*. Proposition 3.5 (p.126) shows that C^{−1}(V′_s,θ′_s) is rigid, and no stated result shows that C(E) is rigid. The fact can be recovered: run the proof of Proposition 3.5 with C and C^{−1} exchanged (D′ is also chosen larger than the degree of M^rig_dR→S, which only that reversed argument uses), or use the count n_dR(X_s)=n_Dol(X′_s) of §3.3. But the printed citation does not prove it. This is a gap; the lemma is true. I checked the repair. σ is well defined only because the E_s^j are pairwise distinct and exhaust the rigid points: Proposition 4.10(c), read as corrected in E9 (the commented-out TeX before (4.2) states this disjointness after shrinking S). A real error in the proof. Published p.140, checked on the page image, same in arXiv v4: 'ι∘ϱ≃ϱ̃⊗χ implies that Tr(ϱ(g))=χ(g)Tr(ϱ̃(g)) for all g∈Γ. Thus, we have χ(g)=1.' Reducing modulo the maximal ideal gives only Tr ϱ(g)=χ(g)Tr ϱ(g). That forces χ(g)=1 where the trace is non-zero and says nothing elsewhere. I checked the Q₈ witness. The 2-dimensional character takes the values 2, −2, 0, 0, 0. Each of the three non-trivial linear characters is trivial on ±1, so ϱ⊗χ≅ϱ; also det ϱ=1 and χ²=1=χ^r. The constant family ϱ̃=ϱ⊗R satisfies the displayed isomorphism with χ≠1, so that isomorphism does not imply χ=1. The proposed repair is right. χ^r=1 puts χ in μ_r(K), so ϱ̃⊗Frac(R)≅(ι∘ϱ⊗χ^{−1})⊗Frac(R) is defined over K. The generic point of Spec R therefore maps to the closed point [ϱ⊗χ^{−1}], so Spec R→M_B is constant, which contradicts non-triviality. Lemma 5.5 is true, and the kind 'error' is right. But 'affects' should be 'the proof', not 'nothing'. PROTOCOL §18 uses 'nothing' for mathematics that is 'right as intended', and here the intended inference is false. Item 092 never states χ=1, so there is nothing in it to correct. Corrected fix: E12: kind error, affects 'the proof' (not 'nothing'), locator 'Proof of Lemma 5.5, p.140'. Use the correction as proposed, with the Q₈ witness in 'reason'. Item 092 needs no change because its statement never uses χ=1. At most, add a clause: 'the PGL⇒GL direction concludes from constancy of ϱ̃⊗Frac(R)≅ϱ⊗χ^{−1}'. Severity: Low is right: the lemma and everything downstream stand.

(1) Example 6.3 (p.146) takes 'α∈Z̄∖μ∞ be an algebraic integer which is not a root of unity such that |α|=1' and defines ϱ into GL₁(Z̄). Let P∈Z[x] be the monic minimal polynomial of α. Complex conjugation fixes the coefficients of P, so ᾱ is a root of P and hence an algebraic integer. Since |α|=1, ᾱ=α^{−1}. So α is automatically a unit, and the example is correct as printed. Item 107 says 'Require α⁻¹ integral as well to land in GL₁(O_Qbar)', and its planningAPI entry inverseIntegral says 'Check α and α⁻¹ are integral'. The extraction's top-level keys are paper, protocol, status, source, summary, conventions, baseline, items, routes, prerequisites, sourceIssues, gaps, notTheorems and verification. There is no sourceVersions, although E1, E2, E4 and E7 have affects 'a stated result'. PROTOCOL §18 says 'The file therefore records what was read, alongside sourceIssues', and it applies that to paper extractions. Two qualifications. First, no checker enforces this for an extraction. check_paper.py never reads sourceVersions, and the versions_checked function in check_errata.py (lines 35–40) runs only on errata files, so the extraction passes its own checker. Second, the rule came after this work: PROTOCOL gained the paragraph in commit eab24c32 (2026-09-24), a day after the review accepted the extraction (commit 45cf910e, 2026-09-23). So this is a retrofit, not an error of the extraction. The omission has a visible effect. The provenance() function in collation.py classifies this record as 'preprint', because its free-text notes mention arXiv and name no publisher host that function recognises. In fact the published PDF was read, and its SHA-256 (0d81a6d3…) reproduces. The proposed values match source.url/sha256 and source.comparison. Corrected fix: Add sourceVersions as proposed. On the author-copy entry, record that it was read only selectively (per source.comparison.read), and note that its 'read' date is inferred from source.accessed.
